items.title: Every finitely branching level tree carries a sequence of ordered partitions with uniform successor numbers
items.author: Supakun Panasawatwong; J. K. Truss
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem produces, for any tree with omega finite levels, a sequence of ordered partitions of its levels such that between consecutive levels the number of successors of a node inside a given piece is the same for all nodes of the piece (statement lines 527-530). The proof runs refinements of the partitions of each level along a schedule in which every level is treated infinitely often, refining one level at a stage by grouping nodes according to the vector of intersection sizes with the pieces of the next level, and ordering the pieces so that each previous piece splits into consecutive parts (proof lines 532-544). The step that carries the content is the limit argument: since each level is finite the refining sequences stabilise, and at the stable stage the grouping relation has become trivial on every piece, which is exactly what makes the successor counts uniform (proof lines 546-551). H2.
